name: Guardian genius crossword No 224
preamble: Eleven solutions (not further defined), when paired with a thematic word, reveal characters (real or fictional) and other things. Wordplay in the remaining 17 clues contains a superfluous letter; these letters generate a cryptic hint (7,2,2,6) as to the theme. Eleven of these 17 clues contain a superfluous word, each defining one of the 11 thematic pairs.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A noted film festival with rubbish support upset actress

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the pair of words upside down, so they read from the bottom

blocks.note: a gala is a festive occasion; one of its letters is the superfluous one
rot is rubbish and aid is support
the superfluous word: with LANCASHIRE it defines the thematic pair SARAH LANCASHIRE

explanation.surface: A celebrated film festival, its rubbish support collapsing, upsets an actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble the wordplay has one spare letter, here the A of GALA, and one spare word, 'actress'. Sarah Lancashire is a British TV actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiator is Ridley Scott's Oscar-winning 2000 epic starring Russell Crowe, so it is a famous movie.

clue.text: Discipline shown by Latin actor on holiday gets to be weaker?

blocks.note: to train is to discipline; its N is the superfluous letter
L is the abbreviation for Latin
the superfluous word: with ESSEX it defines JOEY ESSEX, the reality TV personality
someone off is away from work

explanation.surface: A Latin actor on vacation grows slack in his discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: Spare letter N of TRAIN and spare word 'actor', both as the preamble says. The question mark flags a slightly loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice or sound that trails off fades gradually, growing fainter until it stops, so it weakens.

clue.text: Spanish city largely associated with aromatic plant

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so the city name falls short of its final letter

blocks.note: León is a city in northwest Spain
nard, or spikenard, is an aromatic plant yielding ointment

explanation.surface: A Spanish city known mostly for a fragrant plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Unclued thematic entry: with CHESHIRE it gives LEONARD CHESHIRE, the RAF bomber pilot and charity founder, defined by the spare word 'serviceman' in 18 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Left undefined by the preamble; followed by a northwestern county it names a decorated wartime pilot who founded a disability charity.

clue.text: Winner supported by Iowa

blocks.note: a victor is a winner
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: A champion backed by an American Midwestern state.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supported by' puts the second piece underneath. Unclued thematic entry: with DERBYSHIRE it gives VICTORIA DERBYSHIRE, the BBC presenter, defined by the spare word 'journalist' in 11 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Left undefined by the preamble; followed by a Midlands county it names a well-known BBC news broadcaster.

clue.text: Leading horse facing struggle gets to lack nutrition

blocks.note: the star is the leading performer
the superfluous word: with SUFFOLK it defines the SUFFOLK PUNCH, a heavy draught horse
to vie is to contend; its I is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: The favourite horse, facing a hard contest, goes underfed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading horse' reads as one phrase, but 'horse' is the spare word. The spare letter is the I of VIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to suffer from too little food, going without the nourishment the body needs.

clue.text: Curtail badger on the rise

indicators.note: to curtail is to cut off the tail, so the pestering verb loses its final letter
in a down clue rising means reading upwards, from the bottom of the light

blocks.note: to badger someone is to pester or harass them

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut short pestering that is growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' is the verb, not the animal. Unclued thematic entry: with LANCASHIRE it gives SARAH LANCASHIRE, the TV actress, defined by the spare word 'actress' in 1 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Left undefined by the preamble; followed by a northern county it names a celebrated British television actress.

clue.text: One dealing with records has article for European

indicators.note: the word for an article is put in the place where the European abbreviation stood, one letter traded for another

blocks.note: a clerk keeps an office's records
the indefinite article
standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An archivist acquires a grammatical article to stand for a European.
explanation.walkthrough: Unclued thematic entry: paired with the county KENT it gives CLARK KENT, Superman's alter ego, defined by the stray word 'superhero' in 23 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble leaves this name undefined; joined with a county it names a famous comic-book reporter with a secret identity.

clue.text: Priest shortly acquiring a coarse fabric is one of immense size

indicators.note: shortly means in brief, so the priest word is cut by its final letter
the cut priest word takes in the single letter, holding it inside

blocks.note: a Levite was an assistant to the priests of the Temple
taken as written
harn is a coarse linen cloth; its R is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: A priest briefly takes on rough cloth, a garment for a giant.
explanation.walkthrough: Harn is an old Scots word for coarse linen; per the preamble its R is this clue's spare letter. There is no spare word here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leviathan is the biblical sea monster, so the word now means anything enormous of its kind.

clue.text: Town's secret cheese regularly ignored in the past

indicators.note: dropping letters at a regular interval leaves every second letter of the words in front

blocks.note: the even letters of these words; the S is the superfluous letter
the superfluous word: with DORSET it defines DORSET BLUE VINNY, a blue cheese

explanation.surface: A town's hidden cheese, routinely overlooked in former times.
explanation.walkthrough: The spare word 'cheese' sits inside the wordplay; the spare letter is the S from secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Once as an adverb means formerly, at some earlier time, so it stands for a phrase about bygone days.

clue.text: Director swamped by retrograde foreign currency

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the currency word is read from its end
something swamped is engulfed, so the director's letter sits inside the money word

blocks.note: the naira is Nigeria's currency
D is the abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: A film director drowned by a backward-moving foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Unclued thematic entry: with the county DURHAM it gives ADRIAN DURHAM, a talkSPORT radio host, defined by the stray word 'Presenter' in 28 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Left undefined by the preamble; paired with a northern English county it names a well-known British sports radio host.

clue.text: Observe backward manner in a liberal journalist regarding a public certifier

indicators.note: backward tells us the manner word is read from right to left
the turned manner word goes inside the pair formed by the article and the party letter

blocks.note: to note is to observe; its E is the superfluous letter
taken as written
an air is a manner or bearing
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
the superfluous word: with DERBYSHIRE it defines VICTORIA DERBYSHIRE, the BBC journalist

explanation.surface: A liberal reporter adopts a backward manner when dealing with a notary.
explanation.walkthrough: Spare letter E of NOTE; spare word 'journalist'.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is a lawyer who certifies documents publicly, and notarial is the adjective describing such an official or their work.

clue.text: Australian cricketer with rush into ground sure to be destructive type?

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters of sure are rearranged
into places the first pieces inside the rearranged word

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for Australian
the superfluous word: with DEVON it defines DEVON MALCOLM, the England fast bowler
to bolt is to rush off; its L is the superfluous letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Australian cricketer rushes onto the ground, certain to wreck things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian cricketer' reads as one person, but 'cricketer' is the spare word. The spare letter is the L of BOLT.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately damages or obstructs things, so is literally a person bent on destruction.

clue.text: Ship with perishable cargo avoiding last shoal

indicators.note: avoiding the last means the ship word steers clear of its final letter

blocks.note: a reefer is a refrigerated cargo ship

explanation.surface: A refrigerated cargo vessel steers away from the final sandbank.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the last letter leaves REEFE; per the preamble its spare letter is an E.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoal is a shallow place in the sea, and a reef is a ridge of rock or coral near the surface.

clue.text: By the sound of it, informed on Jones, maybe

indicators.note: this phrase says the first word is chosen for how it is said, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: to blow the whistle on someone is to inform on them
Vinnie Jones, the footballer turned film hard man, is one Jones

explanation.surface: Seemingly someone grassed on a man called Jones.
explanation.walkthrough: Unclued thematic entry: Dorset, a southwestern English county, makes the pair with it, a veined cheese defined by the spare word 'cheese' in 9 down. Vinnie Jones is a footballer turned actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Left undefined by the preamble; preceded by a southwestern county it names a traditional veined cheese made from skimmed milk.

clue.text: Author to own chapter about timeless religious celebrations

indicators.note: timeless means without time, whose usual abbreviation is dropped from the celebrations word

blocks.note: the superfluous word: with SOMERSET it defines SOMERSET MAUGHAM, the novelist
C is the abbreviation for chapter
on means about, as in a book on birds
religious festivals are feasts; one letter of the result is the superfluous A

explanation.surface: An author owns up to a chapter about religious festivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Losing T leaves FEASS, whose A is the spare letter; 'Author' is the spare word.
explanation.definitionFit: To own, as in own up or acknowledge, is to admit something, which is what confessing does.

clue.text: Broadcaster has trouble cutting prize money for military chaplain

indicators.note: the trouble word cuts into the money word, splitting it around itself

blocks.note: Sky is a British TV broadcaster
an ill is a misfortune; one L is the superfluous letter
the pot is the pool of winnings

explanation.surface: A TV channel's troubles eat into the jackpot meant for an army padre.
explanation.walkthrough: Spare letter: one L of ILL. No spare word in this clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky pilot is slang for a clergyman, especially a forces chaplain, as one who guides souls heavenwards.

clue.text: Pass surrounded by mixture of clay and chalk

indicators.note: the mountain-crossing word is enclosed on both sides by the soil word

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass
malm is a soft chalky loam

explanation.surface: A mountain pass hemmed in by chalky clay, a geologist's landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: Unclued thematic entry: after the county DEVON it gives DEVON MALCOLM, the England fast bowler, defined by the stray word 'cricketer' in 12 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Left undefined by the preamble; preceded by a southwestern county it names a famous English fast bowler of the 1990s.

clue.text: Agents might use this canoe serviceman made haphazardly

indicators.note: haphazardly means without order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written; one A is the superfluous letter
the superfluous word: with CHESHIRE it defines LEONARD CHESHIRE, the RAF pilot
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spies might use a canoe that a soldier built carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Either A could be the spare letter; 'serviceman' is the spare word.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret agents operate under assumed designations, cover identities that hide who they really are.

clue.text: Religious official with head obscured concealing a disgusted reaction

indicators.note: with its head hidden, the official's title loses its first letter
the shortened title hides the next pieces inside itself

blocks.note: an imam leads prayers in a mosque
taken as written
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A cleric with face veiled hides his revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: Unclued thematic entry: after SOMERSET it gives SOMERSET MAUGHAM, the novelist, defined by the spare word 'Author' in 15 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Left undefined by the preamble; preceded by a southwestern county it names the writer of Of Human Bondage.

clue.text: Briefly put down detective falling short in both cases

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the writing-down word loses its final letter
falling short means not reaching the end, so the sleuth word loses its last letter too

blocks.note: to jot is to write down quickly
a private eye is a detective

explanation.surface: Someone tersely dismisses an underperforming detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in both cases' says both words are curtailed. Unclued thematic entry: with ESSEX it gives JOEY ESSEX, the reality TV personality, defined by the stray word 'actor' in 2 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Left undefined by the preamble; followed by a home county it names a British reality television personality.

clue.text: Fancy harp on top of nearly outdated machine

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine, so these letters are reimagined in another order
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
this initial is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: Imagine a harp perched on top of an almost obsolete contraption.
explanation.walkthrough: The initial of 'nearly' is the spare letter, so only the shuffled letters of harp on remain.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing, an orphan is a discontinued product its maker no longer supports, left without a parent company.

clue.text: Dane's beer drunk in port

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering and confusion, so the letters before it are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written; the S is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: A Dane gets drunk on beer down by the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The spare letter is the S of Dane's.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a Scottish city and harbour on the North Sea, a major base for the oil industry.

clue.text: Film on country with no end of nostalgia shows what some superhero artists do

indicators.note: with no means without, so the following letter is taken out of the country
the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film
Chad is an African country; its D is the superfluous letter
the final letter of this word
the superfluous word: with KENT it defines CLARK KENT, Superman

explanation.surface: A film about a nation, minus its nostalgia, shows how comic-book artists work.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'what some artists do' once the spare word 'superhero' is removed; the spare letter is the D of CHAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchers engrave designs onto metal plates with acid, so etching is the craft some printmakers practise.

clue.text: Source of humour with Chinese

blocks.note: a pun is wordplay that raises a laugh
CH is an abbreviation for Chinese

explanation.surface: A source of comedy together with Chinese food, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of humour' looks like a definition of the magazine Punch, but this is an unclued thematic entry: after SUFFOLK it gives the SUFFOLK PUNCH, a draught horse, defined by 'horse' in 5 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Left undefined by the preamble; preceded by an East Anglian county it names a breed of chestnut heavy draught horse.

clue.text: Get rid of fish

blocks.note: to dump is to get rid of
the ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An order to throw away the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Unclued thematic entry: after NORFOLK it gives NORFOLK DUMPLING, a boiled dough ball, defined by the stray word 'food' in 26 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Left undefined by the preamble; preceded by an East Anglian county it names a traditional plain boiled dough dish.

clue.text: Chef's first individual food suitable for fatty dish

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: initial letter
one is a single individual; its E is the superfluous letter
the superfluous word: with NORFOLK it defines NORFOLK DUMPLING
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: The chef's first single serving is just right for a rich, greasy plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Spare letter E of ONE; spare word 'food'.
explanation.definitionFit: Confit is meat such as duck slowly cooked and preserved in its own fat, a classic rich French preparation.

clue.text: A location for playing that hosts first of games of many sides?

indicators.note: letters set out for playing are toyed with and rearranged
the rearranged phrase plays host to the next letter, taking it inside
first of picks the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written; the I is the superfluous letter
initial letter

explanation.surface: A sports venue that stages the first of the games has many sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that eight sides is only loosely 'many'. The spare letter is the I of location.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagonal shape has eight sides, a good number of faces, so the setter fairly calls it many-sided.

clue.text: Presenter to alter designation with new degree

blocks.note: the superfluous word: with DURHAM it defines ADRIAN DURHAM, the radio host
a name is a designation; its N is the superfluous letter
N is the abbreviation for new
D is short for degree, as in a doctorate

explanation.surface: A TV host decides to change a title by adding a new qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: Spare word 'Presenter'; spare letter the N of NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to make changes or corrections to something, such as a law or document.
